processing_steps.method: vacuum arc melting followed by 4× remelting (ingot flipped before each remelt)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Two steel compositions (Fe–8Mn–3Al-0.2C = M1 and Fe–8Mn–3Al–1Si-0.2C = M2) were fabricated using a vacuum arc melting furnace; the ingot was remelted 4 times by flipping to ensure complete and uniform melting.

Homogenization of as-cast samples was carried out at 1100 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching. Table 1 labels this state 'Homogenized (1100 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching)' → M1-HQ, and it is the parent process of the hot-rolled condition.

Samples were hot-rolled at 1100 °C to reduce thickness by 50 %, with finish rolling temperatures reaching around 900 °C. Table 1 lists this state as 'Hot rolled (~50 % thickness reduction at 1100-900 °C)' → M1-HR. α-ferrite in M1 steel is expected to form during this step when the finish rolling temperature reaches around 900 °C.
Following hot rolling the samples were air cooled. Formation of martensite in M1 steel occurred during air cooling after hot rolling (as supported by the calculated Ms of 319 °C).

structures.overall_structure: Hot-rolled M1 steel microstructure comprises multiple phases including ferrite, austenite, and martensite. M1 steel exhibits polygonal α-ferrite and a lath-type morphology of martensitic-austenitic (α' + γ) phase. The XRD patterns confirm the presence of ferrite/martensite and austenite phases, with a small austenite fraction (fγ = 5.1 %).

phases_present.morphology: lath-type, present within the martensitic-austenitic (α'+γ) constituent

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: dog bone-shaped specimen, gauge length 2 mm, thickness 1 mm, width 1 mm, machined by wire-EDM
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tinius-Olsen ST25 universal testing machine (UTM) equipped with a 25 kN load cell

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: M1-HR engineering stress-strain curve rises steeply to a peak between the 1500 and 2000 MPa gridlines at ~15 % strain, then drops abruptly (brittle); no stress-strain data reported for the HR condition beyond the UTS and TE values

characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) in secondary electron (SE) mode
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Fig. 4(a1,a2) micrographs of M1-HR at 5 µm and 3 µm scale bars
characterization_methods.purpose: To observe the phase constituents of the hot-rolled M1 steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: M1-HR exhibits polygonal α-ferrite grains and lath-type α'+γ (martensitic-austenitic) regions.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: PANalytical Empyrean instrument with Cu-Kα radiation (λ = 1.542 Å), 2θ range 40–115°, step size 0.03°
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification and quantification of the austenite phase fraction using the direct-comparison method
characterization_methods.key_findings: Confirms the presence of ferrite/martensite and austenite in M1-HR; the austenite (γ) fraction is calculated as 5.1 %.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Systematic Al addition to the Fe–8Mn-0.2C system; lower critical temperature taken as 600 °C to account for limited Mn diffusion at lower temperatures
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicted phases used for alloy design; the 3Al (δ-ferrite-free) composition was selected as M1, consistent with the observed absence of δ-ferrite in M1-HR.

computational_details.simulation_method: Empirical calculation of martensite-start (Ms) temperature from austenite composition
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Elemental concentrations taken corresponding to the austenite phase at hot-rolling temperatures, in wt.%
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Ms of M1 HR sample calculated as 319 °C, supporting the observation of martensite in the M1-HR sample (formed during air cooling after hot rolling).

analytical_models.equation_role: Predict the martensite start temperature (Ms) of the steel from its austenite composition (wt.%): Ms(°C) = 539 - 423C - 30.4Mn - 7.5Si + 30Al
analytical_models.model_note: For M1 (Si-free) the Si term is zero; the calculated Ms for the M1 HR sample is 319 °C, indicating transformation of some austenite into martensite during cooling.

unmapped_findings: Martensite in the M1-HR sample formed during air cooling after hot rolling, consistent with the calculated Ms temperature of 319 °C for M1.
In M1 steel, α-ferrite formation is expected to occur during hot rolling with finish rolling temperatures reaching around 900 °C.
The M1-HR sample displays brittle behaviour with significantly high UTS and very low total elongation; SEM fractography of the fractured M1-HR tensile sample shows cleavage 'flat facets'.
The M1-HR hot-rolled sample contains ~5 % austenite prior to intercritical annealing, in the form of lath-type martensitic-austenitic (α'+γ) phase together with polygonal α-ferrite.
